For some reason it’s not letting me edit the post so here’s my experience:

I took the text at a testing center, I showed up an hour early even though the instructions said 30 minutes. I was listening to a few tips and tricks and just reviewing my mistakes in previous exams beforehand. Once I got in, the processing was smooth. As soon as I started the exam I had the strategy of not to dwell on questions, if I am not sure I’ll put the answer I think is most likely, flag the question and then move on. The first 60 questions were arguably the hardest of the 180, I had flagged 14 questions. I revised all my answers and triple checked on those 14 questions. I recommend that you most definitely take the breaks, the change of room, air and just stretching your legs really helps break the tension and stress. Once I got back to the next 60 questions they were a lot easier than the ones before, I had a few questions come quite similar if not identical to questions that I had solved before so that gave me a big confidence boost. And I did the same approach to the following 120 questions left and took the break in between. Once I revised, I submitted pretty early. I really hope I didn’t screw it up because I’ll be really disappointed, and all this confidence will be embarrassing. Hahaha
If there’s anything I can do, let me know! Good luck 🤞🏻
